The study uses aircraft parameters from Adamson for F-104G and Asselin for F-16C.
The nominal radar detection distance for an aircraft with 1 m² RCS is fixed at 15 km in simulations.
RCS is highly dependent on azimuth and elevation angles relative to the radar station.
The RCS of the Saab 105 model is 12.0 m² in the nose direction, resulting in a detection distance of 27.9 km when heading directly at the radar.
Flight-path angle, heading angle, altitude, velocity, fuel mass, and position coordinates form the state vector in the optimization.
Control variables include thrust setting, angle of attack, and bank angle.
The optimization problem is formulated with algebraic constraints on dynamic pressure, load factor, and radar detection.
Hermite-Simpson collocation is used for discretizing the nonlinear optimal control problem.
The aircraft trajectory is optimized to pass a radar station at 2 km altitude with a maximum altitude constraint of 5 km.
Minimizing detection time alone results in a detection time of about 67.9 seconds for the Saab 105, compared to 299.5 seconds for a direct approach.
Including fuel consumption in the objective increases detection time slightly but reduces fuel usage.
The aircraft tends to fly at maximum altitude for energy buildup before diving to the target to minimize radar exposure.
RCS variations cause many local minima in optimization, making smooth spline approximations necessary.
The study confirms that 3D RCS constraints can be incorporated efficiently into flight-path optimization.
The full 6-DOF flight model is computationally intense, so a simplified model is used for optimization.
Radar detection time is defined as the interval between first detection and reaching the target.

The optimization shows that flight paths avoiding head-on radar exposure can reduce detection distance to near the minimum RCS aspect.
The paper uses a generic RCS model for a small conventional airplane to test the method.
The Jacobian of the RCS constraint is computed analytically from the spline representation for computational efficiency.
